text:
sam: Hey team — user accepted an org invite but gets 403 on console. They can call the API fine with their API key, but console shows 'You do not have access'. Tried hard refresh and new browser, still 403.

marta: Which org/project? can you paste the user email and the project id (sanitized) + a repro step list?

sam: user: j.torres@example.com, org: acme-inc, project: proj-84. Repro steps I followed:
1) sent invite via console
2) user clicked invite link, completed accept flow (ok)
3) when they click "Open console" they land on 403 page immediately
4) API calls using their API key succeed (tokens verified)

I captured the network log from the browser. Here's the failing request header from the console app:```
GET /api/projects/proj-84/permissions HTTP/1.1
Host: console.redwood.ai
Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOi... (ephemeral)
Accept: application/json
```
response: 403 {"error":"forbidden","reason":"role_binding_not_found"}

lee: Hmm — looks like the ephemeral browser token returned at accept time doesn't have the project-role binding applied yet. Could be a race between SCIM/SCOPES sync and the session bootstrap. Did you see any events in ops-bot when the user accepted?

ops-bot: detected event: invite.accepted user=j.torres@example.com org=acme-inc time=6321112230

marta: Can you try one quick repro: after user accepts, force a console sign-out + sign-in (to fetch new session token) OR hit the API that returns /session/refresh. If that fixes it, it's likely a session-latching issue.

sam: Tried that. They signed out, cleared cookies, signed in again — still 403. BUT I did a manual "resync user" from the admin -> members page (DevTools: POST /admin/members/resync {email}) and access was restored immediately.

lee: Good. So root cause hypothesis: delegated-sso flow issues where the accept flow issues an ephemeral token before the membership/role propagation completes, and the console latches that token (session cached) rather than waiting for the role binding write to finish. Manual resync forces the binding to be visible and new session tokens get correct scopes.

marta: Can you collect server logs for the accept flow? Look for two events: invite.accepted (idempotent) and role.bind.create for that user. We want timestamps to see ordering. If role.bind.create is after token mint, that's the race.

sam: Attached snippet of timeline from infra logs (sanitized):

```
6321112229 invite.accepted user=j.torres@example.com via=okta
6321112231 token.mint ephemeral=eyJ... scope=openid profile
6321112235 role.bind.create user=j.torres@example.com org=acme-inc role=project.viewer
6321112237 session.bootstrap completed user=j.torres@example.com
```

lee: That matches the race. token.mint happened before role.bind.create. Console tried to use the ephemeral token (no role) and failed.

marta: Thanks — can we reproduce reliably? If yes, please file a bug and include reproducible steps. Workaround for now: admin resync or remove+reinvite which forces synchronous bind. Also we can try to make the console retry /session/refresh on 403 once after a small backoff.

sam: I can repro locally by creating an invite and intentionally delaying the role.bind.create by ~5s. I'll file the reproduction in the ticket.

lee: I'll open an internal issue: RM-4591 "Invite accept race: ephemeral token latches before role binding" and assign to eng-auth. Proposed short-term fix: console should treat 403 from /permissions on first session bootstrap as "maybe binding not applied yet" and call /admin/members/refresh or /session/refresh then retry once. Long-term: make invite acceptance synchronous for critical role binds or change token minting to wait for bind commit.

ops-bot: ticket created RM-4591 by lee assignee=@auth-team priority=high

marta: Noted. Sam — when you file repro, include the sanitized log block above and steps to delay the bind. I'll send the workaround notes to the support KB and email the customer with the temporary resync steps (admin -> members -> Resync). :thumbsup:

sam: Will do. Customer now has access after I did the manual resync. Leaving thread here, will update RM-4591 with repro steps and a quick patch suggestion for console retry behavior.

lee: Thanks — tagging @platform to watch for any related concurrency issues in role service.

marta: Closing on support side for now, will reopen if customer sees it again."
